name: Cholesteryl Ester Storage Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Cholesteryl Ester Storage Disease

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient lysosomal acid lipase enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the LIPA gene
Evidence of hepatomegaly with hepatic lipid accumulation on liver biopsy or imaging
Presence of mixed dyslipidemia characterized by elevated LDL cholesterol and triglycerides with low HDL cholesterol

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient lysosomal acid lipase enzyme activity plus identification of pathogenic LIPA mutations; supportive clinical and biochemical findings aid diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy is less commonly required due to availability of enzyme and genetic testing

laboratory: Reduced lysosomal acid lipase enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Mixed dyslipidemia: elevated LDL cholesterol, elevated triglycerides, low HDL cholesterol
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatomegaly with fatty infiltration
other: Liver biopsy showing cholesteryl ester and triglyceride accumulation in hepatocytes and Kupffer cells

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in infancy with severe failure to thrive
Near complete absence of lysosomal acid lipase activity
Rapidly progressive course with adrenal calcifications
Absence of lysosomal acid lipase deficiency
Associated with metabolic syndrome and obesity

redFlags: Markedly elevated transaminases without other cause
Early onset mixed dyslipidemia with hepatosplenomegaly
references: Bernstein DL, et al. Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency: Review of the clinical spectrum and therapeutic developments. Clin Lipidol. 2013;8(6):659-672.
